newsitem.title: USA: Videolabs says sees cost-cutting results.
newsitem.headline: Videolabs says sees cost-cutting results.

text.p: Videolabs Inc said Friday its plan to reduce costs, focus on its key markets and introduce a business partner model for distributors has already begun to have an effect on the company.
"We are already seeing the positive impact of the actions in the first two months of the new year," James Hansen, acting president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The company reported a fourth quarter loss of $0.68 a share versus a profit of $0.05 a share last year.

Sales were $1.94 million, down from $2.61 million the previous year. The decline was primarily due to increased competition in Europe and substantially lower sales in Asia. Unit volumes were flat, the company said.
In addition, Videolabs said it has settled a lawsuit with a former officer of the company.

The settlement, combined with the discontinuation of a project, the creation of warranty reserves and staff reductions, led to a $1.9 million charge in the fourth quarter. The charge increased the quarterly loss by $2.1 million and the yearly loss by $2.3 million, Videolabs said.
Videolabs provides image capture and transmission solutions.
